open_points.subject: A10/A11/A14 resend after not_applied authority
open_points.text: A10 rule 1: "A resend after `not_applied` ... needs a fresh approval ... and ... [send] is not a resend after `not_applied`" for grant use; but A11 rule 1 says authority is "... otherwise an approval or a grant" and A14 rule 2 says on resume "... otherwise its unused approval ... or a grant still active".
open_points.question: After `not_applied`, is a standing grant ever allowed to authorize the resend, or is fresh owner approval always mandatory?
options: Fresh approval is mandatory; grant must never authorize that resend.
Grant may authorize resend when active (approval only preferred).
open_points.default_guess: Fresh approval is mandatory and grant is ignored for resend-after-not_applied.

open_points.subject: A08 manifest validation scope for proposal/accept/send checks
open_points.text: A08 rule 5 enumerates failures (missing fields, duplicate capability names, invalid invocability, etc.) but does not define required types/shape for many manifest fields beyond those checks (for example capability entry structure, `required_headers` value types).
open_points.question: Which additional manifest structural/type faults must be treated as manifest mismatch, and at which exact check position in the "first failing" order?
options: Only explicitly listed faults are checked; other malformed shapes are tolerated until later send-time failure.
Any structural/type mismatch needed to build M10/A09 is a manifest mismatch at proposal/accept with deterministic earliest check ordering.
open_points.default_guess: Fail fast: treat any structure/type needed for invocation as manifest mismatch at proposal/accept.

open_points.subject: A09 path placeholder grammar
open_points.text: A09 rule 2: "every `{name}` in the path takes the input port of that name"; no formal grammar is given for what counts as a `{name}` token (nesting, escaping, invalid braces, duplicate placeholders).
open_points.question: What exact parser/grammar defines path placeholders and invalid placeholder syntax?
options: Simple token rule: `{` + port-name + `}` only, no nesting/escaping; invalid brace patterns refuse the binding.
Best-effort string substitution for brace pairs, leaving ambiguous cases implementation-defined.
open_points.default_guess: Use strict placeholder token parsing and refuse ambiguous/invalid brace syntax.

open_points.subject: A01/A03/A09 handling of non-JCS-representable runtime values
open_points.text: A01 rule 1 says non-finite numbers are refused "where [a value] enters"; A03/A09 outcome tables do not explicitly map a function/service output value that validates schema but cannot be canonicalized under JCS.
open_points.question: When runtime output contains a non-JCS value (e.g., NaN/Infinity), which node status/outcome must be recorded?
options: Treat as `contract_violation` at output validation/storage boundary.
Reject only at author-time schema level, making runtime impossible.
